findings.title: A failed multi-file install can change files while reporting that nothing was replaced
findings.affected: Artifact tools/splice.py installation loop and tools/aeneas-std.sh fail diagnostic; explicit --record mode has the clearest mixed-generation consequence.
findings.reproduction: Run check.py install-error. The real two scripts successfully record synthetic sample0. Replace only the fixture's Code.lean destination by a directory, request reviewed recording of sample1, and let the real splice reach its rename phase. This is an ordinary output-path type collision, not a failure injected into os.replace itself.
findings.expected: After an installation error, diagnostics describe the actual state. If unchanged-files behavior is promised for installation failures too, preserve or restore the complete active set.
findings.observed: The wrapper exits1 and logs IsADirectoryError, but still says nothing in lean/ was replaced. Extraction/Funs.lean has changed from sample0 to sample1, earlier targets were installed, Code remains the conflicting directory, and the manifest remains the old one. Temporary siblings can remain after the failed rename.
findings.impact: A local caller investigating a failed regeneration can incorrectly assume the active generated files are untouched. Installation is atomic per file, not transactional across the set. Failure is visible and nonzero; this is not silent successful verification, a false proof, or reopening of AUD-014-BLD001. In default mode the main generated bytes already match the expected baseline, limiting the consequence further.
findings.evidence: install-error-result.json: controlExit0, exitCode1, reportedNothingReplaced=true, funsChanged=true, manifestUnchanged=true, renameErrorSeen=true. Funs SHA256 changes c90126f6ea8cac10da281622ab5ad0e5347076ebcb48e0a017e2ee2beaa03749 →30aa5e796bf8492473b84ce7163ea52b0a1dc157cde6be844b48c0896d0ef7ca. The independent tooling scope confirms the same reachable rename boundary by source inspection.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish pre-install refusal from failed installation and say that installation may be partial when a rename/delete fails. Document per-file atomicity. Full rollback is optional unless an all-or-nothing install guarantee is retained; do not add unnecessary transactional complexity merely to close a diagnostic issue.
findings.requiredVerification: Retain the thirteen translator/baseline scenarios and add a mid-install filesystem-error case. It must return nonzero and report possible partial installation accurately; if rollback is promised, assert every active output is restored. Preserve the real successful output identities.

remediation.evidence: Actual wrapper rejects early/partial/silent translator failures, padded Error-on-exit0 and baseline differences;13 cases pass; genuine Aeneas reproduces all five outputs; explicit recording is separate from baseline checking.
Independent source/document review confirms correct six-adapter plus two-codomain description for all eight R blocks, with unchanged generated lower-level methods and active FnMut scope.
Both documents retain old98620cc target, describe newer3d88078 disclosure/security additions and explicitly exclude the new bounds from this proof.
No target source was edited by this review.
